messages:
Aria: FYI NimbleHealth wants a GA commitment for inference routes. They asked for an SLA, per-route token billing, 24/7 emergency support, and EU data residency for logs. Need a quick triage on scope & tradeoffs.

Ravi: what latency numbers and models? also are they expecting embeddings or generation mostly?

Aria: mostly generation on M-2 family. Target p95 < 180ms for 512 tokens, steady qps ~120, bursts to ~900 for 4-6m. They want logs retained in EU-only for 90 days.

Len: EU log retention + residency is extra infra work (KMS/replication policy). SLA-wise, Dedicated pinned pools + multi-AZ routing looks feasible for p95 but we should quantify tail risk on bursts.

Jo: ops note 1/ SLA language: define latency SLOs vs availability SLOs. Will coordinate with legal on credit calc. Also, per-route token billing changes billing pipeline; need a short spec.

Morgan (sales): commercial context: pilot contract $200k ARR Y1. Customer wants simple SLA bullets to include in their MSA and a short pilot window. They accept limited pilot capacity.

Aria: requirements list I got from Nimble:
- committed p95 latency (180ms)
- 99.9% availability target for their routes
- per-route token billing (examples requested)
- 24/7 emergency support (pager + phone)
- EU-only logs for 90d
- fallback plan that documents quality deltas

Ravi: monitoring / alarms: per-route p50/p95/p99, error-rate, token burn-rate, and SLO burn-rate alert when >50%. Auto rollback rule if p95 > target for 5m. Also sample request/response capture for quality monitoring.

Len: engineering spikes: pinned pool + autoscale for bursts (infra), plus quantized fallback pathway (runtime). Estimate: infra 3w (2 engs), runtime + fallback 2w (1 eng), testing & burn-in 1w. Docs and legal in parallel 1w. Total ~5 weeks if parallelized.

Jo: legal checklist: SLA metric defs, credit formula (we propose credit = min(0.25 * monthly fee, usage-based prorated credits)), cap the total credits, exclusions (maintenance, customer config errors, force majeure). Need clear wording for degradation vs outage.

Len: data residency implications: we'll need to ensure logs never exit EU tenant, and shield telemetry retention in Console UI. Security & infra to estimate.

Aria: two options to propose to customer:
A) Premium Pilot (Dedicated): 99.9% availability + p95 latency objective, per-route token billing, EU log residency, 24/7 emergency support, SLA credits, faster launch (~5w).
B) Standard Pilot (Hosted): 99.5% availability, burst addon for reserved capacity, limited support (business hours + on-call), delayed EU log residency (~Q+1), longer validation (~8w).

Morgan (sales): customer prefers A but needs pricing. If A, we should include a short exit clause after 30 days if SLA not met.

Jo: legal: ok to include 30-day pilot exit + credit cap. Will not accept unlimited credits. Draft clause once we pick numbers.

Ravi: ops guardrails: require traffic ramp over 48h, pre-approved test harness, staging soak, and a rollback trigger (p99 > target for 10m -> failover + page). Also, request customer to provide payload samples and a seq-length histogram.

infra-bot: ticket CREATED: PILOT-1142 "NimbleHealth GA pilot scoping" assigned to @Len @Ravi @Jo

Len: I'll start infra spike for pinned pools; need model versions and sample traces by EOD to begin profiling.

Aria: I'll draft spec doc with the two offer options and sample billing examples for per-route token pricing. Will post draft in 36 hours. Action owners: Aria (spec & docs), Len (infra + tests), Ravi (monitoring & rollback), Jo (legal), Morgan (sales + contract).

Morgan (sales): I'll prepare a short MSA bullet list and confirm customer ok with pilot capacity & exit clause.

Jo: legal will prepare a templated SLA credit clause (cap + exclusions).

Aria: quick team poll 1/ A (Premium Dedicated) or B (Standard Hosted)? react with :one: or :two:.

Morgan (sales): :one:
Len: :one:
Ravi: :one:
Jo: :one:

Aria: consensus for A. We'll proceed with Dedicated pilot plan and align on pricing. Thanks all, reconvene after I post the spec. :white_check_mark:
